I am currently in the middle of doing an "elimination diet" to figure out if the cause of my chronic hives was food related. Basically for the past month, I've not eaten any wheat or wheat products, no dried corn, no peanuts, no dairy, no added sugar, no canola oil, and some other complicated restrictions / ways of eating. If you're super curious, I'm following this program: http://toquietinflammation.com

It hasn't been too difficult. My hives cleared up and my skin looks better overall.

So far I've only tested dried corn. The test was only one day, eating small amounts of things made from dried corn at four out of the five meals of the day. By the end of the day, I had a couple small hives, so I suspect not eating tortilla chips or popcorn will be better for me in the long run.

Will I eat them again? Probably, at some point. But I've got to be back on the elimination phase for a few more days before I can test the next food on the list. That'll be dairy and it's a three day test. After that, peanuts, then wheat. I'm not sure what I'll do after I'm done with all that. Have a beer, perhaps, assuming the wheat test doesn't result in hives as well.

Besides my skin clearing up, I've been losing about 3 pounds a week. Weight loss isn't my primary goal, but I'm happy to see it go.
